summary: claude-study-room is a single-process "Protector" that drives N GitHub repos as boards: every ~20s heartbeat (index.ts:51) it re-ingests open issues into a per-repo TaskMap, fetches issues+open PRs, runs a pure classifier (classify.ts) that emits at most ONE action per board item on a fixed ladder (MERGE>FIX>RESOLVE>REVIEW>PROMOTE>NEEDS_DETAIL>TRIAGE>IMPLEMENT), fair-share-interleaves the per-repo action lists, and dispatches each action onto a "warm worker" chosen by a pure assignment ladder (protector.ts: exact → rerole → cross-repo → spawn → wait). Each dispatched action spawns a `claude -p` process (via the Harness seam) in a fresh per-task git worktree, then commits/pushes and opens or updates a PR via `gh`. Governance (watchdog attempt counters, quarantine + parole, capacity/blackout pauses, contention throttle, file-ownership holds, test-run budget, soft drain) is global and cross-board; item state (taskmap, handled, quarantine, attempts, lifetime, clone, spec) is per-repo in a RepoState bundle (repoState.ts). All durable state lives under C:\Users\pegan\.claude-study-room, one directory per CONFIGURED repo URL with `[/:]` replaced by `-`, plus a handful of global files (engine.log, usage.jsonl, drain.flag, testrun.json, admissions.json). Every key that crosses a board boundary is repo-qualified: `owner/name#7` (flight/task), `owner/name:pr-12` (item), `FIX:owner/name:pr-12` (action). The scheduling/policy brains are genuinely pure and unit-tested (protector, classify, gates, ownership, throttle, assignments, watchdog, parole, schedule, tierFallback, optimizer); everything impure — orchestration, git, gh, process spawn, persistence sequencing, telemetry, reporting — is fused into live.ts, a 2713-line god class with ~45 private methods. The headline gap: the warm-session machinery the whole project exists for (`--session-id` / `--resume --fork-session`, warmCliSession.ts) is wired only into the Editor; the live board loop constructs the Protector with no `attach` hook and passes no session id, so every "warm worker" is in fact a cold `claude -p` run and the ladder's exact/rerole/cross-repo tallies measure warmth that does not exist.

effectiveConcurrency (src/optimizer.ts:35-38): explicit `maxParallel > 0` wins outright; else speed = max(1, base), token = max(1, ceil(base/2)).

Dispatch loop guards, in order (src/live.ts:1367-1424): quarantined action key OR item key → skip; `specMoved()` → parkSpecChanged + skip; `alreadyRunning()` → skip; PROMOTE → runPromote; MERGE → mergeOne; `slots<=0` → skip; file-collision hold via `collidingPaths(claim, claimed)` → skip WITHOUT consuming a slot; then dispatchCli → `slots -= 1`, `watchdog.attempt(item)`, `saveAttempts` + `saveLifetime` immediately.

Assignment ladder (src/protector.ts:197-246): 1 exact (same tier+role+repo, warmest by `lastFinishedSeq`), 2 rerole (same tier+repo, victim = free worker whose current role has least REMAINING demand, tie-break warmest — pickRerole 388-396), 3 cross-repo (same tier, other repo; prefers right role), 4 spawn if `countTier(tier) < perTierMax && workers.length < totalCap` (162-164), 5 wait with reason `tier-at-cap` | `pool-at-cap` (242-245).

Stages (src/taskmap.ts:25-27): `ready | implementing | review | fixing | merging | done`; `readyQueue` requires stage==='ready', no assignedStudent, and every dep at 'done' (taskmap.ts:208-212) and is explicitly LABEL-AGNOSTIC — it cannot see parking labels, which is why live.ts:1040-1057 subtracts parked issues before printing the ingest headline.

Parking labels — the ONE definition (src/classify.ts:166-168): `PARKED_LABELS = [runner-error, spec-changed, needs-human, already-satisfied]`; `isParked()` short-circuits both classifyPull (225) and classifyIssue (259), and a parked ISSUE also suppresses its PR (classify.ts:341-350).

Deadlock detection: `isDeadlocked` = reviewed-ok/APPROVED AND runner-error (classify.ts:189-193); surfaced per board into `rs.deadlocked` and logged once on ENTRY (live.ts:668-685), never auto-resolved.

Merge policy is centralised in gates.ts: `normalizeReviewMode` (39-46) fails CLOSED to 'human' for unrecognised values; `canAutoMerge` = autoMerge && mode !== 'human' (141-145) and is the flag fed to classify; `mergeGate` (56-69) orders review verdict before merge gates. index.ts:36-37 warns at boot via `reviewModeIssue`.

Review verdict parsing: gates.ts:124-133 — last `VERDICT: APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES` wins, keyword fallback, default REQUEST_CHANGES (never approves on ambiguity). postVerdict THROWS if the label write fails (live.ts:2356-2363) because the label is the durable verdict.
Watchdog defaults (src/watchdog.ts:94-112): wedgeTicks 4, fatalWedgeCount 4, fatalErrorStreak 5, maxItemAttempts 9, rewriteAfterAttempts 5, boardChurnLimit 3, probeAttempts 1, lifetimeDispatchCap 15.

Quarantine is two-layered and durable: quarantine.json + a `runner-error` label on the item itself (live.ts:227-290); `quarantineItem` additionally files a deduped GitHub report via `openIssueOnce` to `cfg.reportRepo` (live.ts:296-337). Default reportRepo is `Pat201492/claude-study-room` (config.ts:199).

Parole: a quarantine is a SENTENCE not a life term — `reoffend()` lengthens it, `dueForParole` releases on PROBATION with `watchdog.probe(itemKey)` (1 dispatch), and `lifetimeExhausted` (cap 15) blocks parole permanently (live.ts:763-802, parole.ts).

Capacity handling: `noteCapacityBlocked` parses the CLI's own reset time via `parseCapacityReset(msg, now)` and falls back to the 5-minute flat backoff (live.ts:597-613); GitHub-side all-repo failure uses `githubRateLimitReset()` clamped to [now+30s, now+1h] (live.ts:1212-1221) and calls `tickOk()` — never `tickError()` — so an outage cannot kill the engine.

Infra failures (CLI never started) reuse `capacityFailed` so reconcileWatchdog forgives BOTH the no-progress counter and the attempt budget (live.ts:624-636, 1663-1671); `infraStreak` resets on any student that completes (live.ts:2118).

Throttle (src/throttle.ts): contention = RESOLVE dispatches + re-dispatches this tick (live.ts:1364,1411-1412,1429); >contentionThreshold(1) shrinks the effective cap by 1, 3 consecutive clean ticks grow it by 1, never above the operator ceiling.

File-ownership hold (#177): `claimsFiles` = IMPLEMENT|FIX|RESOLVE only (live.ts:1437-1439); claim = issue's `Owns:` globs for an issue, PR's changed `files` ∪ its issue's owns for a PR (1445-1461); collisions computed by `collidingPaths` and held without consuming a slot; held claims persist in `inFlightFiles` keyed by action key and are pruned via `keyInFlight` (1355-1357).

Fair share across repos: `fairShare(byRepo, offset)` (classify.ts:86-102) walks RANKED_KINDS, round-robins repos within each rank, and rotates the starting repo by an incrementing cursor (live.ts:1556-1558).

Soft stop: drain.flag file (drain.ts) checked EVERY beat (not latched) so cancelling resumes without restart (index.ts:307); `busy = inFlight.size + reviewing.size + merging.size` (live.ts:1079-1081); drainComplete clears the flag then exits 0 (index.ts:276-283). `merging.delete` is in a `finally` because leaving it made busy===0 unreachable (live.ts:1840-1867).

Bounded test run: `noteTestRunUnit` counts 'pr' or 'merge' completions and, when the budget is spent, clears testrun.json and calls `requestDrain()` — reusing the soft stop rather than a second stop concept (live.ts:1097-1108).
Blackout window: `inBlackout(new Date(), cfg.blackout)` holds dispatch, logs only on the edges, and returns before dispatch (live.ts:1265-1282); config.json currently sets 22:00-23:00 enabled.

Harness seam: `getHarness(id = 'claude-code')` throws on an unknown id rather than falling back (harness.ts:137-144); registry populated by importing harnesses.ts (harnesses.ts:21-24, registers claude-code and opencode). Every call site in live.ts calls `getHarness()` with NO id — config-driven harness routing is not wired.

Harness run options actually passed by live.ts: `{onUsage, cwd, model: cfg.pool[tier].model, permissionMode, claudeBin, tools: cfg.studentTools, onIdleKill, budget?: cfg.studentBudget?.implement, onBudgetStop?}` (live.ts:1899-1909, 2171-2184, 2298-2308, 2445-2455, 2566-2576). No `sessionId`, `resume`, or `forkSession` anywhere in live.ts.

Per-task worktrees are created fresh per dispatch: implement → `addWorktree(rs.clone, 'study/issue-<n>')` (live.ts:2163-2165), review → `study/review-issue-<n>` (2292-2294), fix/resolve → `addWorktreeForBranch(rs.clone, pr.headRefName)` (2422, 2541); all clone-level git is serialized through `lockGit` (live.ts:221-225).

PR branch convention: `study/issue-<n>`; the issue behind a PR is parsed from the head branch by `pullIssueNumber` (classify.ts:125-128, regex `issue[-/](\d+)`) and `issueNumFromBranch` (live.ts:99-102).

Progress signature used by the watchdog: PR = `${mergeable}|${statusCheckRollup}|${reviewDecision}|${sortedLabels}`; issue = `issue|handled=<bool>` (live.ts:1579-1586). Same key + same signature after an attempt finishes = no progress → bump.

releaseConverged (live.ts:1620-1641): any quarantined PR that has since earned `reviewed-ok` is released, its attempt + lifetime counters cleared, and its `runner-error` label removed — run FIRST inside reconcileWatchdog.
reconcileUnparked (live.ts:720-753): an item whose parking label a human removed is returned to the board mid-run (no restart), released on PROBATION via `watchdog.probe`, not a full budget reset.

sweepCarveOuts (live.ts:437-474) parks carve-out children whose parent was closed as COMPLETED by a PR, BEFORE a dispatch is spent; sweepReports (live.ts:391-418) closes watchdog reports whose subject item has left the board, throttled by `sweepDue`.

Empty-diff handling: `classifyEmptyRun(result.text)` — 'satisfied' → parkAlreadySatisfied (label + comment, never auto-close); 'blocked'/'unknown' → stage back to 'ready' for retry (live.ts:2223-2237).

Triage flow: the student PROPOSES, the orchestrator FILES — `parseTriage` → openIssue per piece → `expectedDifficulty(auditSignals(...))` label per child → `addIssueDeps(parent, filed)` → comment → `EPIC_LABEL` on the parent; aborts and leaves the issue intact if fewer than 2 pieces filed (live.ts:1894-2010).

Attribution matrix is role × tier in memory (`AttributionCell {tasks, tokens, cost, cacheReadTokens, cacheInputTokens}`, pool.ts:38-46) and is NOT persisted; the durable spend record is usage.jsonl via `recordUsageToStore` (live.ts:2072-2099).

snapshot() (live.ts:2641-2692) returns `{running, students: [active…, warm…], attribution, protector: AssignmentSnapshot, parallelism:{effective, configured}, boardHealth:{deadlocked, parked}, capacity?:{pausedUntil, reason}}`; idle workers are rendered from `protector.pool` with last-known token/cache values.

AssignmentLog (assignments.ts) is a pure ring buffer, `MAX_RECENT = 200`, tallies `{exact, rerole, crossRepo, spawn, wait, total, warmReuseRate}` where warmReuseRate = (exact+rerole+crossRepo)/placed and waits are excluded from the denominator (assignments.ts:118-127).

boot() (live.ts:824-846): builds a RepoState per configured slug under the SAME root (`dirname(statusDir)`), then per repo `bootOne`: ensureClone → reapOrphanWorktrees → ensureLabels → readSpec → loadQuarantine → seedAttempts (disk + `rejectedReviewCount` per open PR) → ingest → reconcileHandled (boot-only, deliberately).

readSpec (live.ts:964-989) deliberately does NOT send CLAUDE.md (the CLI injects it; measured +14,531 tokens for a 56,558-char file) — only a guard telling the student not to re-read it — and sends docs/SPEC.md only when it differs from CLAUDE.md.

Test suite: 58 test files under test/, run with `node --import tsx --test test/*.test.ts` (package.json). The pure modules each have a dedicated test (protector, classify, gates, ownership, assignments, fairShare, repoState, parole, schedule, drain, probeBudget, releaseConverged, crossRepoKeys, specCollision, sharedCursor, statusSnapshot…). No test file targets live.ts as a whole.

config.json defaults (config.ts:186-200): repo '', optimizationMode 'token', reviewMode 'auto', maxConcurrent 4, pool {haiku/sonnet/opus maxWarm 3}, claudeBin 'claude', permissionMode 'bypassPermissions', reportRepo 'Pat201492/claude-study-room'. pain_points.issue: The warm pool is not actually warm in the live board loop. The Protector is constructed with NO `attach` hook (live.ts:206-211) and no live.ts harness call passes sessionId/resume/forkSession (1899-1909, 2171-2184, 2298-2308, 2445-2455, 2566-2576), so every dispatch is a cold `claude -p`. `Worker.worktree` (protector.ts:46,175) is never read — worktrees are created per task by addWorktree. warmCliSession.ts is imported only by editor.ts.
pain_points.evidence: grep across src/: `warmCliSession` appears only in editor.ts:5,365; no `sessionId`/`forkSession` in live.ts; `this.protector` usage in live.ts is limited to rebalance/assignOne/finish/pool (lines 1323, 1772-1773, 1804-1830, 2133, 2659-2678).

pain_points.issue: live.ts is a 2713-line god class: ~45 private methods mixing orchestration, git, gh, process lifecycle, persistence, telemetry, GitHub issue authorship (report bodies as inline string arrays), and dashboard snapshotting. No test targets it directly; every pure rule it depends on had to be extracted elsewhere to be testable at all (classify.fairShare's comment at classify.ts:82-85 records that the test previously asserted a hand-copied duplicate).
pain_points.evidence: wc -l src/live.ts = 2713 (145,589 bytes); test/ has 58 files, none named live*.test.ts.

pain_points.issue: `saveHandled()` always persists the PRIMARY repo (live.ts:814-816 `persistHandled(this.rs)`), but runTask calls it after mutating a possibly-secondary repo's set (live.ts:2207-2208 `rs.handled.add(n); this.saveHandled();`). A secondary board's handled.json is therefore never written, so after a restart its already-PR'd issues are not remembered (only the live open-PR fetch prevents a re-dispatch).
pain_points.evidence: live.ts:814-816 vs live.ts:2207-2208; contrast with saveQuarantineFor(rs) which exists precisely for this reason (live.ts:267-271).

pain_points.issue: `parkSpecChanged` mutates the ACTION's repo state but persists the primary's: `const rs = this.rsFor(a); … rs.quarantined.add(item); this.saveQuarantine();` — saveQuarantine() writes this.rs (live.ts:263-265). A spec-changed park on a secondary board survives only in memory.

`this.rs` is a mutable cursor that boot swaps in and out (`bootRepo`: save prev, assign rs, restore in finally) purely so synchronous helpers like loadQuarantine/saveHandled can find 'the current repo'. The file's own comments admit this only works by an ordering accident and that the same pattern already caused a cross-board data corruption on 2026-08-14.
pain_points.evidence: live.ts:881-900 (bootRepo + the bootOne docblock), live.ts:994-1004 (the ingest docblock), index.ts:285-302 (the re-entrancy guard added in response).

pain_points.issue: status.json is written to the PRIMARY repo's dir only (index.ts:53-56, 76) while snapshot() aggregates students, boardHealth and assignments across every repo (live.ts:2673-2691). The dashboard reads the same single path (dashboard.ts:107). Secondary repos' state dirs contain a stale or absent status.json (verified: several repo dirs have no status.json at all).
pain_points.evidence: index.ts:53-56; dashboard.ts:107; on-disk: fitworks/PoolWorks/cardworks dirs have taskmap.json + attempts.json but no status.json.

pain_points.issue: Protector capacity is frozen at construction. perTierMax/totalCap are computed once from cfg.maxConcurrent and pool[*].maxWarm (live.ts:204-211) and protector.ts exposes no setter, so changing pool sizes in the dashboard has no effect until restart — even though the engine re-reads config.json every beat and Throttle.setCeiling IS updated per tick (live.ts:1340).

reconcileWarm(), healthCheck(), recycle(), and sleep() — the health/recycle half of the advertised Protector — are never called from src/ (only from test/protector.test.ts). Nothing ever pre-warms, parks asleep, or recycles a wedged worker in production; workers only ever go busy→idle-warm.
pain_points.evidence: repo-wide grep for reconcileWarm/healthCheck(/.recycle( matches only protector.ts definitions and test/protector.test.ts.

pain_points.issue: Double GitHub fetch per ingest tick: `ingest(rs)` calls fetchIssues (live.ts:1007) and then the classify loop immediately calls fetchIssues again for the same repo (live.ts:1158). On a 15s re-ingest clock against a 20s heartbeat this roughly doubles issue-list API calls on most ticks.

The Task Map is advertised as the editable plan but is overwritten wholesale from GitHub every ingest (`rs.taskMap = fresh; saveTaskMap(...)`, live.ts:1008-1015). Dashboard edits — priority, pinned, role, added deps — are lost within 15 seconds; only `stage` is partially reconstructed (from inFlight/handled). In live mode the map is a derived cache, not a plan.
pain_points.evidence: live.ts:1008-1015; taskmap.ts:86-130 edit ops exist for a map nothing preserves; pool.ts:200-213 documents the opposite contract for sim mode.

pain_points.issue: Telemetry mis-attribution on multi-repo: rebalance records and the warm map are stamped with `repoSlug(cfg.repo)` (the primary board) regardless of which board's demand drove them (live.ts:1325, 2678), even though the per-assignment record was fixed to use `this.rsFor(a).slug` (1780).

Four near-identical role runners (runTask 2161-2243, runReview 2288-2332, runFix 2417-2505, runResolve 2537-2627) each re-implement: worktree add → harness run with the same 7 options → recordUsage → prState staleness check → commit/push → removeWorktree in finally. runRole (2105-2136) factored out only the register/deregister/free skeleton; the ~100-line bodies stayed duplicated and have already drifted (the resolve path historically skipped the pool-grid token update — fixed at 2578-2584 with a comment saying so).
pain_points.evidence: live.ts:2020-2026 explicitly documents the copy-paste and the drift it caused.

pain_points.issue: BoardAction is extended by casting: the repo stamp is attached as `{...a, repo: rs.slug}` (1167-1168) and read back via `(a as BoardAction & {repo?: string}).repo` (1531), and synthetic actions are built with `as unknown as BoardAction` in five launch* methods. The repo field is load-bearing for every key, yet it is not in the type.

Two disagreeing definitions of 'what will run': classify() honours parking labels, readyQueue() cannot see labels at all (taskmap.ts:200-207). live.ts works around it by subtracting parked issues when printing the ingest headline (1040-1057) — a per-caller patch rather than one source of truth.

v2_implications: KEEP VERBATIM the pure core: protector.ts, classify.ts, gates.ts, ownership.ts, throttle.ts, assignments.ts, parole.ts, schedule.ts, tierFallback.ts, optimizer.ts, plus the key helpers from repoState.ts. These are already the shape v2 wants (no clock, no IO, caller-supplied `at`), carry incident-derived rules that would be expensive to rediscover, and ship with real tests. Port them first and let the new orchestrator be written against them.

KEEP the key vocabulary exactly: `owner/name#7` (flight/task), `owner/name:pr-12` (item), `KIND:owner/name:pr-12` (action). Three distinct counters key off the item vs action distinction (no-progress ladder on actions, oscillation cap and lifetime cap on items) and collapsing them re-opens two bugs the comments document (a fix↔review ping-pong that no per-action counter can see; a quarantine deleted one tick after it was written because trackedItems() returned qualified keys matched against bare ones).

KEEP the on-disk contract if v2 must run against existing boards: per-repo dir named from the CONFIGURED URL with `[/:]`→`-`, containing taskmap.json / handled.json (number[]) / quarantine.json (parole records, legacy string[] tolerated) / attempts.json / lifetime.json / repo/ / worktrees/. attempts and lifetime MUST stay separate files (repoState.ts:224-228 explains: a widened attempts.json silently drops the ceiling for an older engine).

DECIDE FIRST whether v2 is a warm-pool engine at all. Today it is not: the live loop spawns a cold `claude -p` per action and the Protector is pure bookkeeping. Either (a) wire warmCliSession into the dispatch path — give Worker a real session id, pass `--session-id` on first use and `--resume --fork-session` after, and make the worker's worktree its own rather than per-task — which makes the exact/rerole/cross-repo ladder mean something; or (b) drop the warm-pool framing and keep the Protector purely as a fair, cap-respecting (tier, role) allocator. Shipping the current middle state means the project's headline claim is unmeasured, and `warmReuseRate` in status.json is currently a number about nothing.

RE-CUT live.ts along the seams it already implies, with the repo made explicit instead of ambient. Suggested split: (1) BoardCycle — fetch/classify/fairShare/dispatch-loop, pure over an injected GitHub port; (2) RoleRunner — ONE parameterised runner (prompt builder, worktree strategy, post-run effect) replacing runTask/runReview/runFix/runResolve/runTriage; (3) Governance — watchdog + quarantine + parole + capacity + blackout + throttle, taking and returning decisions rather than performing IO; (4) Persistence — every save*() takes the RepoState it writes; (5) Reporting — the GitHub issue bodies currently inlined as string arrays. Delete `this.rs` entirely: pass RepoState as a parameter everywhere (bootOne/ingest/reconcileHandled already do, and their docblocks explain why).

MAKE the repo a typed field on BoardAction (and on the fetched PR) instead of a cast-on cast-off property. Every multi-repo bug listed in live.ts's comments — wrong task map consulted, wrong ledger read, report filed against the wrong repo, assignment attributed to the wrong board — is the same defect wearing different clothes, and it recurs because the type system was opted out of at the stamp site (live.ts:1167) and the read site (1531).

FIX the three remaining primary-repo leaks during the port, not after: saveHandled (live.ts:814), parkSpecChanged's saveQuarantine (369), and the rebalance/warmMap repo stamps (1325, 2678). Also make status.json either per-repo or explicitly one aggregate file at the root — the current 'aggregate content at the primary repo's path' is neither.

MAKE runtime reconfiguration uniform. Throttle.setCeiling is updated every tick; Protector caps are not; the Task Map is overwritten from GitHub every ingest. v2 should state, per knob, whether it is operator-owned (config, survives ingest), derived (recomputed each tick), or hybrid — and enforce it. Concretely: if Task Map pinning is meant to be a control surface, pins must be merged into the freshly ingested map, not clobbered by it.

KEEP the governance ladders and their asymmetries — they encode real money. Fast-shrink/slow-recover throttling; forgive-don't-charge for capacity and infra failures (with the attempt BUDGET refunded, not just the no-progress counter — live.ts:1655-1671); release on probation (1 dispatch) rather than a full budget reset; a lifetime dispatch cap that parole cannot launder; park-don't-close for already-satisfied work; never auto-resolve a reviewed-ok+runner-error deadlock. Each of these has a dated incident attached in-comment.

KEEP the classifier's one-action-per-item invariant and its ordering (NEEDS_DETAIL > TRIAGE > IMPLEMENT; parked issue suppresses its PR; epic is a tracker never a unit of work). Derive any second ordering (the multi-repo walk) from RANK rather than restating it — classify.ts:72-73 already does this and explains why.

KEEP the harness capability model (declared, inspectable, unknown-id-throws, fidelity derived from capability) but CLOSE its leak: HarnessRunOptions is currently an alias of cliStudent's RunCliTaskOptions, so `claudeBin` and the Claude-specific option surface are baked into the interface. v2 should define a harness-neutral run options type with an escape hatch for harness-specific flags, and actually route `cfg.harness` through getHarness(id) so the second adapter is reachable.

KEEP prompt/spec economics: do not re-send CLAUDE.md (the CLI injects it; +14.5k tokens measured for one repo), keep the anti-re-read guard, keep sending docs/SPEC.md only when it differs, keep the tool allowlist (measured -11,382 tokens/turn), keep budgetStop banking partial work. These are the measured wins and none of them live in the parts worth rewriting.

DROP or quarantine the sim: pool.ts carries a full random-walk student simulator (tick(), spawnStudent, STAGE_FOR_ROLE) that exists only to demo the dashboard, yet PoolState/Student/AttributionMatrix — the types the live engine and dashboard both depend on — live in the same file. Split the shared types out of the simulation before porting, or v2 inherits Math.random() in its core type module.

DECIDE the single-process-N-boards rule deliberately: the comment at live.ts:818-823 and repoState.ts:9-19 argue correctly that N engines cannot share an account-wide rate limit. Keep one process, one budget, N RepoStates — and make that structural in v2 (a Board array owned by an Engine) rather than a Map bolted beside a legacy `rs` cursor.

ADD the test level that is missing: every pure rule is tested and the 2713-line integrator is not. v2's orchestrator should be written so the tick is a pure function of (board snapshot, state, clock) → (decisions), with effects applied by a thin executor — which makes the heartbeat itself testable and would have caught the primary-repo persistence leaks above.
open_questions: Is the warm-session gap intentional (deferred as #125/#121, both referenced as still open in protector.ts:20-25) or a regression? protector.ts states plainly that the repo spec is loaded into `this.spec` and 'nothing consumes it', which would make cross-repo reuse free — but readSpec's output IS passed into every prompt (taskPrompt/reviewPrompt/…), so the comment and the code now disagree.

Should status.json be per-repo or one aggregate at the state root? snapshot() is already cross-repo; the dashboard reads one primary path; secondary repo dirs have no status.json at all. Which way v2 goes changes the dashboard contract.
Are the legacy `Pat201492-<repo>` state dirs still read by anything (editorAll.ts:60 builds slug-form dirs for the Editor), or are they dead and safe to drop in v2's migration?

What is the intended lifetime of `admissions.json`, `admissions-split.log`, and the top-level *-dryrun.ts scripts (ac-tiering-dryrun, admissions-dryrun, audit-dryrun, blocked-impact, card-dryrun, park-propagation, relabel-issues, untriage-oversized)? They are outside src/ and were not in scope here, but several read the same state dirs.
Does anything besides index.ts consume drain.flag, and does the dashboard's 'Start pool' path always clearDrain() before spawning (drain.ts:39-48 says both startPool and drain-complete should)?

Is `maxParallel` meant to override the optimizationMode entirely (optimizer.ts:35-38 says yes) while `maxConcurrent` still feeds warmTargets/perTierMax? Today config.json sets both to 2, so the interaction is untested in production.

Should MERGE and PROMOTE really be exempt from the slot budget? They cost no model tokens but do cost GitHub API calls and can cascade (a merge re-conflicts every open PR, which is precisely what the throttle exists to damp).
Is the `default/` state dir (last written 2026-07-08, sim-mode status.json) still produced by any current path, or purely historical?
